hero.headline: Total solar eclipse set to cross Europe and parts of North America Wednesday
hero.body:
A total solar eclipse will occur on August 12, 2026, with the path of totality crossing parts of Europe and offering partial visibility in some U.S. states. The event comes one day after multiple news outlets began tracking the eclipse's approach, providing viewers across multiple continents the opportunity to witness the celestial phenomenon.

The path of totality will primarily traverse Europe, where observers in the direct path will experience complete darkness as the moon passes between Earth and the sun. The Guardian reported that Europe will see the total eclipse, with specific guidance on the best viewing locations and safety protocols for watching the event. CNN detailed how scientists map the path of totality, the narrow corridor where observers can witness the complete blocking of the sun.

In North America, some U.S. states will be positioned to see a partial solar eclipse, where the moon will cover only a portion of the sun. Al Jazeera provided a solar eclipse tracker indicating specific times the eclipse will reach different locations on August 12. WLWT confirmed that certain U.S. states will have visibility of the partial eclipse later this week.

The event represents a significant astronomical occurrence, as total solar eclipses visible from populated land areas are relatively rare. Observers in the path of totality will experience the full eclipse effect, including the dramatic dimming of daylight and the appearance of the sun's corona, the outer atmosphere normally invisible due to the sun's brightness. Those viewing partial phases will see the moon take a bite-shaped section out of the sun's disk.

Safety experts emphasized the importance of proper eye protection when viewing any phase of the eclipse. Looking directly at the sun without appropriate solar filters can cause permanent eye damage. Special eclipse glasses that meet international safety standards are required for direct viewing, while indirect viewing methods such as pinhole projectors offer safe alternatives for observing the event.

cards.headline: Iran escalates demands over Strait of Hormuz as Trump faces Middle East challenges
cards.teaser: President Trump confronts pressure from Iran, which is asserting strategic advantage over the Strait of Hormuz and increasing its demands.
cards.body:
President Trump is pursuing sanctions as a strategy to pressure Iran, as diplomatic talks have stalled and U.S. weapons stockpiles have declined. The administration is betting that increased pressure can force a breakthrough in negotiations.

The escalating tensions have created security concerns significant enough that Trump was moved via a secret plane swap during a NATO summit in Turkey, with reporters initially told he remained on Air Force One.

cards.headline: Russia strikes Ukraine with North Korean missiles, Zelensky says
cards.teaser: Ukrainian president says ballistic missiles from Russia's ally were used in strikes on Zaporizhzhia that killed at least six people.
cards.body:
Russia carried out overnight attacks on the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia using ballistic missiles supplied by North Korea, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The strikes killed at least six people and injured 19 others.

The attacks underscore deepening military cooperation between Moscow and Pyongyang amid Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine.

cards.headline: Syrian court sentences Assad to death in absentia for war crimes
cards.teaser: The ousted Syrian dictator was convicted of committing war crimes and crimes against humanity during the country's civil war.
cards.body:
A Syrian court has sentenced former president Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia for war crimes and crimes against humanity. The conviction stems from actions committed during Syria's 14-year civil war, which resulted in approximately half a million deaths.

Al-Assad was ousted from power and is no longer in the country. His brother was also sentenced to death in the same trial, which proceeded without either defendant present.

cards.headline: Colombia earthquake kills over 100 as rescue efforts continue
cards.body:
A powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia, killing more than 100 people and causing extensive damage across the country. The tremor, which hit at 7:34 a.m. local time on Monday, was the strongest recorded in Colombia in a decade.

The earthquake's epicenter was located in the western department of Chocó. The shaking was powerful enough to be felt across the border in neighboring Venezuela, a country still recovering from a deadly double earthquake that occurred on June 24.

The quake caused severe destruction in major cities including Cali and Pereira, where numerous buildings collapsed or sustained significant damage. Rescue teams mobilized across affected regions to search through collapsed structures for survivors who may be trapped in the rubble. The scale of the destruction prompted a major deployment of emergency personnel and resources to coordinate search and recovery operations.

The death toll climbed to at least 132 people as assessments continued, with dozens more injured from the powerful tremor. The widespread devastation led authorities to declare a state of emergency as they worked to understand the full extent of damage across the country.

Colombia's geological survey, working alongside the US Geological Survey, confirmed the 7.4-magnitude measurement. This made it one of the largest earthquakes to strike the country in recent years and tested the nation's emergency response infrastructure significantly.

The earthquake represents one of the deadliest natural disasters to affect Colombia in recent years. Rescue operations faced the challenging task of locating and extracting people from damaged buildings, particularly in urban areas where building collapses were most severe.

Authorities coordinated resources and personnel across multiple affected areas as emergency crews continued their search through the night and into subsequent days. The mobilization of rescue workers reflected the serious nature of the disaster and the urgent need to locate survivors before critical time windows closed.

Recovery and rebuilding efforts are expected to require considerable time as the full scope of damage becomes clearer. Damaged infrastructure, collapsed homes and buildings, and disrupted services will need systematic assessment and repair. The impact on the country's economy and communities will likely be significant given the magnitude of destruction and loss of life.

The earthquake added to a difficult period for the region, which had already been affected by other natural disasters. The focus for authorities and emergency responders remained on immediate life-saving efforts while beginning the longer process of assessing damage and planning reconstruction across the affected areas of Colombia.

cards.headline: Nvidia partners with Wall Street firms to mobilize over $500 billion for AI infrastructure
cards.body:
Nvidia has partnered with six major Wall Street financial institutions to establish financing platforms aimed at mobilizing over $500 billion in third-party capital for artificial intelligence infrastructure projects. The partners in this arrangement are Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR.

The capital will support the development of new data centers designed to house and operate the extensive arrays of computer chips required for AI computing. These facilities demand substantial investment due to the enormous power and cooling requirements of modern AI systems. The data centers will contain miles of stacked computer chips that process the computational workload necessary for AI applications.

This financing arrangement comes as Wall Street financial firms position themselves to capitalize on the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence technology. By collaborating with Nvidia, the dominant manufacturer of AI processing chips, these institutions gain exposure to the AI sector through infrastructure investments. The partnership structure allows the financial firms to pool capital and distribute both investment requirements and potential returns across multiple parties.

For Nvidia, the arrangement provides access to significant capital for expanding AI infrastructure without bearing the complete financial burden independently. The company continues to dominate the market for AI chips, with its graphics processing units serving as the standard hardware for training and running artificial intelligence models. The partnership extends Nvidia's influence beyond chip manufacturing into the broader ecosystem of AI infrastructure development.

The announcement arrives during a period of intense scrutiny surrounding AI investment levels. Market analysts have closely watched for signs that major technology companies might reduce their spending on AI infrastructure. However, Nvidia recently reported financial results that exceeded investor expectations. The company posted $57.01 billion in total revenues, surpassing expectations of $54.9 billion. Datacenter sales reached $51.2 billion, beating predictions of $49 billion. CEO Jensen Huang addressed concerns about an AI bubble during the company's earnings call, stating that "from our vantage point, we see something very different" and emphasizing Nvidia's capabilities across multiple phases of AI development.

Some investors have expressed concern that the artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout could represent a speculative bubble similar to the internet stocks of 1999. Recent weeks saw shares in Nvidia and other AI companies decline more than 10 percent from their peaks, with broader market selloffs reflecting these anxieties. Despite these concerns, analysts note that major technology companies remain extremely profitable and continue reinvesting billions of dollars into data centers, servers, and chips. The Wall Street financing partnership represents continued confidence in sustained demand for AI infrastructure across industries as companies integrate artificial intelligence into their operations.

cards.headline: Gold approaches $4,500 an ounce amid oil price surge and inflation concerns
cards.teaser: Gold prices touched $4,400 an ounce and are positioned to rebound further as rising oil prices renew inflation-risk trading.
cards.body:
Gold prices have climbed to over a two-month high, approaching $4,500 an ounce. The precious metal touched $4,400 as traders shifted focus to upcoming U.S. inflation data and reassessed risks related to Iran and Federal Reserve policy.

Rising oil prices have revived inflation-risk trading strategies that favor gold. Investors are monitoring geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and their potential impact on monetary policy, with energy market volatility supporting gold's recent strength.

cards.headline: Ukrainian air strikes kill growing number of Russian civilians
cards.teaser: Ukraine has expanded its air campaign against Russian targets, leading to increased civilian deaths and discontent among Russians.
cards.body:
Russian civilian deaths have risen rapidly as Ukraine expanded the tempo of its air strikes against targets inside Russia. The increased strikes have generated discontent among the Russian population.

The higher rate of Ukrainian attacks represents an escalation in the air campaign. Whether the expanded strikes will alter the Kremlin's approach to the war remains uncertain.

cards.headline: Trump secretly switched planes in Turkey amid Iran missile threat
cards.teaser: The US president used a military jet to leave a NATO summit in Turkey after security concerns about an Iranian threat.
cards.body:
President Trump departed Turkey on a secret military flight following a NATO summit in Ankara, while the public believed he was traveling on Air Force One. The switch was prompted by an Iranian assassination threat against the president.

As part of the security operation, Trump boarded the original Air Force One in view of cameras before being secretly transferred to a smaller aircraft. He was transported via an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and supplies before flights. Reporters traveling with the president were told he remained aboard Air Force One during the departure.

cards.headline: Russia strikes Ukraine with North Korean missiles, Zelensky says
cards.teaser: Ukrainian president says ballistic missiles from Russia's ally were used in strikes on Zaporizhzhia that killed at least six people.
cards.body:
Russia carried out overnight attacks on the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia using ballistic missiles supplied by North Korea, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The strikes killed at least six people and injured 19 others.

The attacks underscore deepening military cooperation between Moscow and Pyongyang amid Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine.

cards.headline: Disinformation on social media fueled Spain-Morocco migrant crisis
cards.teaser: A wave of online disinformation contributed to a surge of migrants in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, resulting in about 90 deaths.
cards.body:
A surge of migrants attempting to reach Europe through the Spanish enclave of Ceuta resulted in approximately 90 deaths. The crisis was fueled in part by disinformation spread on social media, which encouraged people to attempt the dangerous crossing from Morocco.

The disaster highlighted the real-world consequences of false information circulating on social platforms. Following the crisis, Spain introduced temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures amid ongoing irregular migration pressure in the region.

cards.headline: Speculation swirls over Morocco's role in Ceuta migrant surge
cards.teaser: Unproven rumors suggest Morocco may have organized a recent border disaster, possibly influenced by Israel and the United States.
cards.body:
Unverified speculation has circulated that Morocco organized a recent migrant surge at the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, potentially at the urging of Israel and the United States. Experts say the rumors remain unproven.

The speculation reflects the complicated historical relationship between Spain and Morocco in the region. The theories have been amplified despite lacking evidence, according to analysts familiar with the area's dynamics.

hero.headline: Alabama holds second primary election after congressional map redraw
hero.body:
Alabama voters in several congressional districts returned to the polls Tuesday for a second primary election, months after the state redrew its congressional maps in May. The unusual August primary follows the redistricting process that shifted district boundaries and created new electoral matchups.

The delayed primary affects voters in multiple districts who already participated in an earlier round of voting before the maps were redrawn. State officials pushed the affected primaries to August to allow time for the new district lines to take effect and for candidates to file in their newly configured districts.

Election officials have expressed concern that confusion over the two-primary system could suppress voter turnout. Many voters may not realize they need to vote again, or may be unclear about whether their district is among those holding the August contest. The compressed timeline between the map redraw and the second primary has also limited opportunities for voter education and outreach.

The redistricting came after legal challenges to Alabama's previous congressional maps. The May redraw reshaped several districts across the state, requiring a reset of the primary process for those areas. Voters who cast ballots in the original primary will see different district configurations and potentially different candidate options on their August ballots.

Turnout figures from Tuesday's voting will indicate whether the concerns about voter confusion materialized. The winners of the second primary will advance to the general election in November, joining candidates from districts that completed their primaries earlier in the year. Alabama election officials have not indicated whether measures will be implemented to prevent similar two-primary situations in future redistricting cycles.

cards.headline: Midwife works across Alabama to serve mothers in areas without delivery hospitals
cards.teaser: A Black midwife provides care to pregnant women in Alabama counties that lack labor and delivery facilities.
cards.body:
Research from the March of Dimes shows that more than half of counties across the United States have no hospitals offering labor and delivery services. These areas, known as maternity deserts, force pregnant women to travel long distances to give birth and limit access to prenatal care.

One Black midwife in Alabama has responded by traveling across multiple counties to provide maternity care to mothers who would otherwise face significant barriers to healthcare. Her work addresses both the geographic gaps in hospital coverage and aims to improve outcomes for Black mothers and babies, who face higher rates of maternal and infant mortality nationwide.

cards.headline: Primaries in Minnesota and Wisconsin test strength of progressive candidates
cards.teaser: Competitive primary races will measure whether far left candidates can succeed in November general elections.
cards.body:
Competitive Democratic primaries in Minnesota and Wisconsin will measure the electoral viability of progressive candidates, following similar contests in Michigan the previous week. These races pit the party's progressive and moderate wings against each other, with implications for the general election strategy.

In Minnesota, Lieutenant Governor Peggy Flanagan, a progressive, is competing against U.S. Representative Angie Craig for the Democratic Senate nomination. Immigration enforcement has emerged as a key issue in the race, particularly after two state residents were killed by immigration agents during a winter surge.

cards.headline: Former Syrian President Assad sentenced to death by Syrian court
cards.teaser: Bashar al-Assad and his brother received death sentences in absentia for war crimes during Syria's civil war.
cards.body:
A Syrian court has sentenced former President Bashar al-Assad and his brother to death in absentia for war crimes and crimes against humanity. The convictions stem from atrocities committed during Syria's 14-year civil war, which killed approximately half a million people and displaced millions more.

Assad fled Syria after losing power and now lives outside the country. The trial proceeded without his presence in court.

cards.headline: Ukraine says Russia used North Korean missiles in deadly Zaporizhzhia strikes
cards.teaser: President Zelensky reported that ballistic missiles from North Korea were used in attacks that killed at least six people.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia used North Korean ballistic missiles in overnight strikes on the city of Zaporizhzhia. The attacks killed at least six people and injured 19 others, according to Ukrainian officials.

The strikes underscore Russia's reliance on weapons from its ally North Korea as it continues military operations in Ukraine. Zelensky's statement directly links the missiles to North Korea, highlighting how Russia is drawing on international partnerships to sustain its war effort.

cards.headline: Reports say Trump used catering truck to secretly switch planes over Iran threat
cards.teaser: The president reportedly hid in a catering vehicle to move between aircraft after a NATO summit in Turkey.
cards.body:
President Trump departed Turkey on a secret military flight after a NATO summit, while the press corps believed he was aboard Air Force One. The elaborate deception was prompted by an Iranian assassination threat against the president.

According to reporting from the Washington Post and New York Times, Trump boarded the visible Air Force One jumbo jet in front of television cameras, then was secretly transported minutes later via an airport catering container to a smaller military aircraft. The ruse successfully concealed his actual travel plans and location from observers.

cards.headline: Anne Hathaway responds to social media speculation about pregnancy
cards.teaser: The actress addressed critics who questioned whether her baby bump was real at a recent premiere.
cards.body:
Anne Hathaway responded to social media users who suggested her baby bump did not look real during a recent premiere appearance. The actress addressed the theories circulating online that questioned the authenticity of her pregnancy.

Hathaway poked fun at the speculation in her response. The comments came after observers analyzed photos from the premiere and shared their doubts on social media platforms.

cards.headline: Americans refinance mortgages to pay off credit card debt as home equity reaches record levels
cards.teaser: Rising home equity has prompted many Americans to refinance their mortgages to manage mounting credit card debt.
cards.body:
Home equity in the United States has climbed to record levels, leading many homeowners to refinance their mortgages as a strategy to pay down other debts. The surge in home values has created substantial equity cushions for property owners, providing a financial resource to tap when facing other obligations.

Many Americans are using mortgage refinancing to consolidate and pay off credit card debt, which has been mounting. By refinancing, homeowners can access their home equity at mortgage interest rates, which are typically lower than credit card rates, allowing them to reduce their overall debt servicing costs.

cards.headline: Wall Street futures subdued as hopes fade for Strait of Hormuz agreement
cards.teaser: U.S. stock futures traded lower as prospects dimmed for a diplomatic resolution regarding the Strait of Hormuz, with investors awaiting inflation data.
cards.body:
U.S. stock market futures showed muted activity as optimism faded over a potential agreement regarding the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices extended gains amid the ongoing tensions in the Middle East, with the lack of a diplomatic breakthrough contributing to energy market volatility. Major indexes ticked lower, with technology shares coming under particular pressure.

Investors are awaiting the release of Consumer Price Index data, which will provide fresh insight into inflation trends. The combination of geopolitical uncertainty and anticipation of economic data kept futures markets in a cautious stance. Iran negotiations remain unresolved, adding to market uncertainty.

cards.headline: Gold approaches $4,500 an ounce amid oil price surge and inflation concerns
cards.teaser: Gold prices touched $4,400 an ounce and are positioned to rebound further as rising oil prices renew inflation-risk trading.
cards.body:
Gold prices have climbed to over a two-month high, approaching $4,500 an ounce. The precious metal touched $4,400 as traders shifted focus to upcoming U.S. inflation data and reassessed risks related to Iran and Federal Reserve policy.

Rising oil prices have revived inflation-risk trading strategies that favor gold. Investors are monitoring geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and their potential impact on monetary policy, with energy market volatility supporting gold's recent strength.

cards.headline: Businesses invest in climate adaptation as extreme weather events intensify
cards.teaser: Repeated heat waves, wildfires, droughts, and storms are forcing companies to recognize that new climate adaptation investments are unavoidable.
cards.body:
A summer marked by climate-related disruptions has solidified the business community's understanding that investments in climate adaptation are necessary. Repeated heat waves, wildfires, droughts, and storms have created what observers are calling a season of climate misery, prompting companies to reassess their infrastructure and operational strategies.

Businesses across sectors are confronting the need to adapt their operations to withstand increasingly frequent and severe weather events. The recognition that such extreme weather will continue has shifted corporate planning from viewing climate adaptation as optional to seeing it as an unavoidable cost of doing business in a changing climate.

cards.headline: Over 10 companies pay up to $100,000 monthly for early access to Truth Social posts
cards.teaser: Trump Media has launched a service allowing firms to pay for fast access to posts on Truth Social, seeking a new revenue stream amid quarterly losses.
cards.body:
More than 10 companies are paying up to $100,000 monthly for fast-track access to Truth Social posts. Trump Media launched the paid service this month as it seeks to generate new revenue despite posting quarterly losses.

The service allows firms to view content on the platform before it becomes available to general users. The company views the offering as a meaningful income source.

cards.headline: UK councils to receive expanded powers to limit vape and betting shops
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced that local councils will gain additional authority to control the proliferation of vape and betting establishments.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced plans to give local councils greater powers to restrict vape shops and betting establishments in their areas. He highlighted how town centres have deteriorated over decades, arguing that stronger local control over these businesses is needed.

The expanded powers will enable councils to have more discretion when approving or rejecting licenses for vape and betting shops. The government aims to address concerns about the concentration of these retailers in town centres and their effect on local communities and economic vitality.

cards.headline: Perseid meteor shower reaches peak viewing Wednesday night
cards.teaser: The annual Perseid meteor shower will reach its peak Wednesday night, offering observers the best chance to see shooting stars across the night sky.
cards.body:
The Perseid meteor shower will peak Wednesday night into Thursday morning, offering excellent viewing conditions across the northern hemisphere. Astronomers expect 50 to 100 meteors per hour during the peak, making it an ideal time to observe the annual celestial event.

The meteor shower coincides with a total solar eclipse visible across Spain, Iceland and Greenland, as well as a six-planet parade. However, the best time to view the Perseid fireballs will occur after the eclipse ends.

cards.headline: Apple tests photo authentication feature in iOS 27 beta
cards.teaser: Apple is developing a photo authentication system that would verify images came directly from an iPhone camera, according to code found in iOS 27 beta releases.
cards.body:
Apple is working on a photo authentication tool that would confirm whether an image was captured by an iPhone camera, according to references discovered in the iOS 27 beta. MacRumors reported that the feature, labeled 'Apple Reference Image,' appeared in the latest beta version of the operating system.

9to5Mac confirmed that Apple is developing a method to authenticate that photos originated from iPhone cameras. Engadget noted the feature may be introduced with iOS 27, while Cryptopolitan reported that Apple tested the photo authentication capability in iOS 27 beta 5. The tool would provide a way to verify image authenticity at a time when digital manipulation and artificial intelligence-generated images have become increasingly sophisticated.

cards.headline: OpenAI completes $7 billion employee tender offer
cards.teaser: OpenAI has reportedly finished a $7 billion tender offer allowing employees to sell company shares to investors.
cards.body:
OpenAI completed a $7 billion employee tender offer, according to reports. The tender offer allowed current and former employees to sell their shares in the artificial intelligence company to outside investors.

The transaction represents one of the largest employee liquidity events in the technology sector. Tender offers provide employees holding company stock the opportunity to convert their equity into cash without the company going public through a traditional initial public offering.

cards.headline: Mars rock returns to its home planet aboard Perseverance rover
cards.teaser: A Martian meteorite discovered in Oman now serves as a calibration target on the Perseverance rover, returning to Mars after being blasted off the planet by an ancient impact.
cards.body:
A dark rock discovered on the gravel plains of Oman has been identified as a Martian meteorite. The stone was ejected from Mars by an impact event and eventually landed on Earth, where researchers found it.

NASA incorporated the meteorite into the Perseverance mission as a calibration target for the rover's scientific instruments. The rock provides a reference point with known Martian composition, helping scientists calibrate their readings as Perseverance analyzes other rocks and soil samples encountered on Mars.

cards.headline: Study details moon formation from catastrophic planetary collision
cards.teaser: Earth's moon formed after a Mars-sized world collided with the young Earth, blasting material into orbit that coalesced into the lunar body, according to research on the leading formation theory.
cards.body:
Earth's moon is unusually large relative to the planet it orbits, and the leading scientific explanation involves a catastrophic collision in the early solar system. A world roughly the size of Mars struck the young Earth, ejecting material into orbit that eventually formed the moon.

Space Daily reported on the giant impact hypothesis, which remains the primary explanation for the moon's formation and unusual characteristics. The collision would have occurred approximately 4.5 billion years ago during the solar system's formation period. The impact ejected enough material into Earth's orbit to form a body large enough to become spherical under its own gravity.

cards.headline: Alpha Centauri system 4.24 light-years away remains beyond current spacecraft capabilities
cards.teaser: The closest star system to Earth would take about 75,000 years to reach with current spacecraft technology, though proposed laser sail concepts could reduce travel time to decades.
cards.body:
Alpha Centauri, humanity's closest star system at 4.24 light-years away, presents a formidable challenge for space exploration. Using current spacecraft technology, reaching this stellar neighbor would take approximately 75,000 years.

Emerging propulsion concepts like laser sails offer a more promising alternative, potentially cutting travel time to just decades. The system contains Proxima b, an exoplanet orbiting within Proxima Centauri's habitable zone.

hero.headline: Fulham sign midfielder Shea Charles from Southampton for £30 million
hero.body:
Fulham completed the signing of midfielder Shea Charles from Southampton in a transfer deal worth up to £30 million. The club confirmed the acquisition of the young midfielder as part of their squad reinforcement ahead of the new season.

Charles joined Southampton's academy system and developed through their youth ranks before breaking into the first team. The midfielder's performances at Southampton attracted interest from multiple Premier League clubs during the transfer window. Fulham moved decisively to secure his signature in what represents a significant investment in their midfield.

The £30 million fee includes performance-related add-ons that could increase the total value of the transfer. Charles signed a multi-year contract with Fulham, committing his future to the West London club. The transfer represents one of the more substantial deals of the current transfer window for both clubs involved.

Southampton will use the funds from the sale to reinvest in their own squad as they continue their rebuild. The club has been active in the transfer market, both buying and selling players as they reshape their roster. Charles becomes the latest player to depart St Mary's Stadium during this window.

Fulham manager will integrate Charles into the squad during the remaining pre-season preparations. The midfielder is expected to compete for a starting position in central midfield, adding depth and quality to Fulham's options in that area of the pitch. The club views Charles as a player who can contribute immediately while continuing his development at the Premier League level.

cards.headline: Everton and Crystal Palace complete McNeil-Johnson swap deal
cards.teaser: Everton and Crystal Palace finalized a player exchange involving Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson.
cards.body:
Crystal Palace and Everton have completed a straight swap deal involving Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson. Both players have signed four-year contracts with the option of an additional 12 months.

Johnson joined Palace in January from Tottenham for £35m but is now moving to Everton, while McNeil departs Goodison Park for Palace. The deal comes six months after a previous proposed transfer of McNeil to Palace fell through.

cards.headline: Unusual scoring play causes lengthy delay in Red Sox-Blue Jays game
cards.teaser: A rare rule interpretation led to an extended stoppage during the game between Boston and Toronto.
cards.body:
The Red Sox and Blue Jays experienced a lengthy delay during their game after an unusual run-scoring play required officials to review the rulebook. The bizarre sequence prompted umpires to halt play while they consulted with league officials to determine the correct ruling. The play involved a scoreboard error that created confusion about whether a run should count.

Charles McAdoo hit a home run for the Blue Jays, who ultimately won the game 2-1. The victory handed the Red Sox their third consecutive loss. The strange rule quirk that caused the delay became a talking point among fans and observers who witnessed the uncommon situation unfold during the contest.

cards.headline: Liverpool defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe limited to friendly matches only
cards.teaser: Teenage defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe has impressed during Liverpool's pre-season but faces restrictions on competitive play.
cards.body:
Ifeanyi Ndukwe emerged as one of the main storylines during Liverpool's pre-season campaign, but the 18-year-old defender can only participate in friendly matches. The teenage center back's performances during exhibition games drew attention from fans and observers tracking Liverpool's summer preparations.

Ndukwe's restriction to friendly matches stems from registration or eligibility rules that prevent him from appearing in competitive fixtures. The young defender has used the pre-season period to showcase his abilities and gain experience training with Liverpool's first team squad. His performances have raised questions about when he might become available for official competition.

cards.headline: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca discusses replacing Pep Guardiola
cards.teaser: New Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca addressed the challenge of succeeding Guardiola and his use of AI technology.
cards.body:
Enzo Maresca has addressed the challenge of succeeding Pep Guardiola as Manchester City manager in his first extended interview since his appointment. The Italian discussed his coaching philosophy and how he plans to maintain the club's high standards while establishing his own identity.

Maresca has revealed his interest in artificial intelligence and how he incorporates technology into his coaching methods. He is also working through a captaincy decision as he evaluates which player should wear the armband for City.

cards.headline: Trump opposes potential removal of FIFA president Gianni Infantino
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump weighed in on FIFA leadership, calling any move to oust Infantino a mistake.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump has publicly backed FIFA president Gianni Infantino, warning that removing him would be a "terrible mistake." Trump described Infantino as "fantastic" in a post on Truth Social.

Infantino has faced mounting pressure following his failed plan to sell stakes in the men's World Cup to private investors. The FIFA president has led the organization since 2016.

cards.headline: Rory McIlroy commits to FedExCup Playoffs opener in Memphis
cards.teaser: Rory McIlroy confirmed his participation in the FedEx St. Jude Championship at TPC Southwind.
cards.body:
Rory McIlroy committed to playing in the FedExCup Playoffs opener at the FedEx St. Jude Championship in Memphis. The tournament field was set with nearly 70 players scheduled to tee off at TPC Southwind for the first event of the playoff series.

The FedEx St. Jude Championship marks the beginning of the PGA Tour's postseason, where players compete for position in the season-long points race. McIlroy's presence adds star power to the field as golfers navigate the Tennessee heat during the late summer tournament. Tournament organizers prepared for challenging weather conditions as competitors begin their playoff campaigns.

hero.headline: Anne Hathaway Responds to Social Media Theories About Pregnancy
hero.body:
Anne Hathaway addressed social media speculation about her pregnancy after critics suggested her baby bump appeared fake at a recent premiere. The actress responded to the theories circulating online, which questioned the authenticity of her appearance.

The speculation emerged following a public appearance where Hathaway displayed her pregnancy. Social media users posted comments analyzing the appearance of her baby bump, leading to theories that it might not be real. The actress chose to directly engage with the criticism rather than ignore it.

Hathaway has been promoting her new film "The End of Oak Street," a family horror movie in which she stars alongside Ewan McGregor. The film involves survival themes and required the cast to sustain intense performances. First reactions to the dinosaur-themed movie have called it the biggest surprise of the summer.

This is not the first time celebrities have faced public scrutiny over their pregnancies on social media. The practice of analyzing and commenting on pregnant women's bodies has become increasingly common online, with critics often questioning various aspects of celebrity pregnancies. Such speculation has drawn criticism from those who argue it represents an invasion of privacy and perpetuates unrealistic standards.

The actress has continued her promotional work for "The End of Oak Street" despite the online commentary. In interviews, she has discussed her experience working on the horror film and bonding with the cast during the production. The movie represents a significant project in her current slate of work as she prepares for the arrival of her child.

cards.headline: Football YouTuber John Nellis Joins Strictly Line-Up
cards.teaser: The content creator, who has 20 million followers for videos featuring soccer stars, will appear on the British dance competition.
cards.body:
John Nellis, a football-focused YouTuber with 20 million followers, has joined the cast of Strictly Come Dancing. Nellis has built his following through videos featuring prominent soccer players including Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi.

The addition of Nellis represents the show's continued effort to include social media personalities alongside traditional celebrities. His large online following brings a significant digital audience to the dance competition series.

cards.headline: RTL Group Reports Nearly 4% Revenue Increase as Streaming Expands
cards.teaser: The European media company posted growth in its streaming division while linear television and content production revenues declined.
cards.body:
RTL Group posted first-half revenue of €2.9 billion ($3.3 billion), representing a 3.9% increase. The European media conglomerate's streaming business drove growth during the period.

The company experienced mixed results across divisions, with streaming expanding while linear television and its Fremantle content business saw declining revenues. RTL's acquisition of Sky Deutschland from Comcast in June bolstered its overall financial performance.

cards.headline: Travis Barker Documentary About Plane Crash Survival Set for Release
cards.teaser: The film chronicles the Blink-182 drummer's near-death experience and recovery from a 2008 aviation accident.
cards.body:
A documentary titled "Louder Than Fear" about Travis Barker's survival of a plane crash will premiere on streaming platforms this week. The film documents the Blink-182 drummer's near-death experience and the aftermath of the aviation accident.

Barker was involved in a plane crash in 2008 that killed four people and left him with severe burns. The documentary explores his recovery process and return to performing. The trailer shows Barker discussing the physical and emotional toll of the experience.

cards.headline: House of the Dragon Actor Fabien Frankel to Star in Short Film
cards.teaser: The British actor, known for playing Ser Criston Cole in the HBO series, joins the debut project from director Olivier Huband.
cards.body:
Fabien Frankel will star in "Love Unlimited," the debut short drama from actor-turned-director Olivier Huband. Frankel currently appears in "House of the Dragon" as Ser Criston Cole, a knight character in the HBO fantasy series.

The role represents a departure from Frankel's work on the high-profile streaming show. Huband previously acted in "A Discovery of Witches" and "Becoming Elizabeth" before moving into directing.

cards.headline: Calvin Demba Assembles Cast for Second Short Film Directing Project
cards.teaser: The Supacell star has lined up George MacKay, Louisa Harland, Nathalie Emmanuel, and Eric Kofi Abrefa for "The Animals."
cards.body:
Calvin Demba has assembled a cast for his second short film as director, "The Animals." The British actor, writer, and director, best known for the Netflix series "Supacell," will work with George MacKay, Louisa Harland, Nathalie Emmanuel, and Eric Kofi Abrefa on the project.

MacKay recently appeared in "Rose of Nevada" and "Sense and Sensibility," while Harland is known for "Renegade Nell" and "Derry Girls." Emmanuel gained recognition through "Game of Thrones." The casting represents a significant ensemble for a short film production.

cards.headline: Blueface and Chrisean Rock Stopped by Police in San Diego
cards.teaser: Authorities pulled over the two artists for equipment violations during a night out.
cards.body:
Blueface and Chrisean Rock were pulled over by police in San Diego for equipment violations, according to law enforcement. The traffic stop occurred during a night out with their son, Chrisean Jr.

Video footage captured the interaction between the couple and police officers. The stop was related to vehicle equipment issues rather than any other alleged offenses. The two artists were seen together after a period of separation.

hero.headline: Senate Republicans back Thune after Trump declines to endorse leader for another term
hero.body:
Senate Republicans are publicly backing Majority Leader John Thune after President Trump declined to endorse the South Dakota Republican for another term leading the chamber. GOP senators say they will support Thune's continued leadership, even if Trump decides to back a challenger.

The disagreement between Trump and Thune centers on the legislative filibuster, a procedural rule that requires 60 votes to advance most bills in the Senate. Trump has pushed for eliminating the rule to allow Republicans to pass legislation more quickly, while Thune and other Senate Republicans have resisted the change, arguing it protects minority party rights and the long-term function of the chamber.

The public rift marks a significant moment in Republican Party dynamics, testing whether institutional loyalty within the Senate can withstand presidential pressure. Thune's refusal to abolish the filibuster has put him directly at odds with Trump, who views the rule change as necessary to efficiently advance his legislative agenda.

Senate Republicans' decision to openly support Thune despite Trump's opposition demonstrates that some members of the conference are willing to assert independence from the White House. Their backing suggests that legislative experience and institutional relationships carry meaningful weight against presidential influence, at least within the Senate Republican conference.

Recent events have shown the tension between Trump and Senate Republicans on other issues as well. When some GOP senators voted with Democrats on war powers measures related to Iran, Trump criticized them harshly during a Capitol Hill lunch. Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, who voted with Democrats initially, faced particularly heated criticism from the president, who had previously endorsed a rival candidate against him in a primary.

After receiving a White House briefing on Iran from Vice President JD Vance and Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff, Cassidy changed his position and voted against a second war powers resolution. Senator Rand Paul of Kentucky also shifted his vote, saying he wanted to give the president space to negotiate. Trump later thanked both senators and Thune for the outcome, indicating he was satisfied with their reversal.

The contrasting situations highlight the complicated relationship between Trump and Senate Republicans. While some senators like Cassidy have been willing to adjust their positions after direct pressure and White House engagement, Thune appears to have maintained his position on the filibuster despite Trump's opposition.

Whether Trump will follow through on supporting a primary challenger to Thune remains uncertain. If he does, it could set up a significant battle over the future of Senate leadership and define how much influence a president can exert over the upper chamber. The outcome could reshape how Senate Republicans balance loyalty to the president against their own institutional priorities and traditions.

cards.headline: Trump maintains pressure on U.S. Attorney Pirro as Reflecting Pool prosecutions collapse
cards.teaser: President Trump continues questioning the future of U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro after criticizing her handling of cases related to the Reflecting Pool.
cards.body:
Todd Blanche, Trump's former personal lawyer, has been sworn in as U.S. Attorney General following Senate confirmation. Blanche, who served as acting attorney general since April, is the second Senate-confirmed attorney general of Trump's second term.

Trump recently acknowledged that his administration's $14 million renovation of the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool was rushed, with the contractor cutting corners to meet a July 4 deadline. Despite conceding these construction shortcomings, Trump blamed vandals for damage to the Washington landmark, characterizing the resulting harm as confined to a small area.

cards.headline: Iran escalates demands over Strait of Hormuz as Trump faces Middle East challenges
cards.teaser: President Trump confronts pressure from Iran, which is asserting strategic advantage over the Strait of Hormuz and increasing its demands.
cards.body:
President Trump is pursuing sanctions as a strategy to pressure Iran, as diplomatic talks have stalled and U.S. weapons stockpiles have declined. The administration is betting that increased pressure can force a breakthrough in negotiations.

The escalating tensions have created security concerns significant enough that Trump was moved via a secret plane swap during a NATO summit in Turkey, with reporters initially told he remained on Air Force One.

cards.headline: Homicide rates drop 17% in major U.S. cities through first half of 2026
cards.teaser: Violent crime continues declining across the nation's largest cities, with homicides down more than 17% from the same period in 2025.
cards.body:
Violent crime kept falling across many of the nation's largest cities through June, with homicides down 17.2% from the first half of 2025, according to preliminary data from the Major Cities Chiefs Association. The decline now spans two presidencies, beginning under President Biden after the pandemic-era surge and continuing under President Trump.

Trump came into office casting America as being overrun by crime at a time when the numbers were already declining. The sustained decrease in violent crime and homicides represents a continuation of trends that began during the previous administration.

cards.headline: White House uncomfortable with conservative criticism of Ocasio-Cortez egg freezing announcement
cards.teaser: Some Republicans, including White House officials, express concern over conservative backlash to Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's decision to freeze her eggs.
cards.body:
When Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez posted a video giving herself a shot in preparation to freeze her eggs, she instantly injected issues of fertility, family and feminism into political discourse. Some of the online backlash from the conservative right is making Republicans, including some in the White House, a little nervous.

The New York Democrat's Instagram announcement dominated social media and furthered speculation that Ocasio-Cortez is plotting a future presidential run. Her video, in which she preemptively said people would be weird about her decision, sparked extensive online discussion about reproductive choices and political implications.

cards.headline: Progressive candidates face tests in Wisconsin and Minnesota Democratic primaries
cards.teaser: Democratic primaries in two Midwest states pit progressive challengers against moderate candidates in contests that could shape midterm strategy.
cards.body:
Progressives are facing crucial tests in Wisconsin and Minnesota primaries as Democrats weigh their party's direction ahead of the midterm elections. In Wisconsin, democratic socialist Francesca Hong has surged in the Democratic primary for governor, raising party concerns about whether far-left candidates can succeed in the general election.

Minnesota voters are similarly weighing moderate versus progressive options in key races. Lieutenant Governor Peggy Flanagan, a progressive, is competing against U.S. Representative Angie Craig for the Democratic Senate nomination. These primaries reflect broader Democratic questions about electability and the viability of progressive candidates in competitive races.

cards.headline: Memory chip prices surge as AI demand drives electronics costs higher
cards.teaser: Memory chip prices are skyrocketing due to AI demand, pushing up costs for smartphones, laptops, and cloud storage.
cards.body:
Memory chip prices are skyrocketing, thanks to AI demand, and there is no end in sight. Chipflation is pushing up the prices for electronic goods like smartphones and laptops, as well as the costs for cloud storage and hardware.

While the overall effect on inflation may not be huge, as other kinds of products get more weight in the government's measure of consumer prices, the scale of price increases in the semiconductor sector helps explain the eye-popping ascents in semiconductor stock prices. The sustained demand from artificial intelligence applications continues to drive chip costs upward.
